kind: "package-reference""},{"id":"p3s1","text":"# dsh-web-fetch-fakeip"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"English | 中文"},{"id":"p5s1","text":"A drop-in replacement for `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-fetch-http` that keeps the
`web_fetch` tool working "},{"id":"p5s2","text":"when the machine's DNS runs in **fake-ip** mode behind
a transparent-proxy (TUN) setup — with fake-i"},{"id":"p5s3","text":"p left enabled and **no**
`http_proxy` / `https_proxy` / `all_proxy` environment variables."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"## Summary"},{"id":"p7s1","text":"`dsh-web-fetch-http` resolves every hostname itself and refuses the request
unless every answer is a"},{"id":"p7s2","text":" public unicast address. Under fake-ip mode, mihomo and
[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"### Why `198.18.0.0/15` rather than the `198.18.0.1/16` default"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"mihomo's documented default is `198.18.0.1/16`, which is a subset of
`198.18.0.0/15`. The wider bloc"},{"id":"p9s2","text":"k is the RFC 2544 benchmarking range as a whole,
so the default covers both spellings and the neighb"},{"id":"p9s3","text":"ouring block that some
configurations use. Narrowing it to `/16` is safe if you prefer to be strict."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"## What changes, and what does not"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"| Destination | Behaviour |"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"| Hostname whose answers are **all** fake-ip placeholders | **Accepted**, pinned as-is; the connecti"},{"id":"p12s2","text":"on reaches the TUN adapter and the proxy resolves the real origin |
| Hostname resolving to public u"},{"id":"p12s3","text":"nicast | Accepted, exactly as the stock provider |
| Hostname resolving to private / loopback / rese"},{"id":"p12s4","text":"rved | **Refused** (`WEB_BLOCKED_URL`), exactly as the stock provider |
| Hostname with a **mixed** "},{"id":"p12s5","text":"answer set (placeholder + any real address) | **Refused** — never partly accepted |
| IP **literal**"},{"id":"p12s6","text":" in the placeholder block (`http://198.18.0.100/`) | **Refused** — a literal states a destination an"},{"id":"p12s7","text":"d never takes the fake-ip path |
| IP **literal** that is private/loopback/link-local (`127.0.0.1`, "},{"id":"p12s8","text":"`192.168.1.1`, `169.254.169.254`, `10.0.0.1`, `[::1]`) | **Refused** |
| IP **literal** that is publ"},{"id":"p12s9","text":"ic (`1.1.1.1`) | Accepted through the normal validated path |"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"Everything else is inherited unchanged from the stock provider: same-origin-only
redirects, byte and"},{"id":"p13s2","text":" character caps, `Content-Type` classification, charset
decoding from the `Content-Type` header, rej"},{"id":"p13s3","text":"ection of binary types and of URLs
carrying credentials, and the same `WebError` codes (`WEB_INVALID"},{"id":"p13s4","text":"_URL`,
`WEB_BLOCKED_URL`, `WEB_FETCH_TOO_LARGE`, `WEB_FETCH_TIMEOUT`,
`WEB_REDIRECT_BLOCKED`, `WEB_U"},{"id":"p13s5","text":"NSUPPORTED_CONTENT_TYPE`, `WEB_ABORTED`,
`WEB_PROVIDER_ERROR`)."},{"id":"p14s1","text":"## How it works"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"`HttpFetchProvider` accepts a resolver as its second constructor argument —
that is the whole seam. "},{"id":"p15s2","text":"This plugin passes a resolver that understands fake-ip
and lets the stock class do everything else:"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p17s1","text":"The resolver's decision, per answer set:"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"1. Resolve once (or take the literal as stated).
2. Reject malformed entries (`WEB_PROVIDER_ERROR`)."},{"id":"p18s2","text":"
3. If the hostname was **not** a literal and **every** answer is a placeholder
in a configured bloc"},{"id":"p18s3","text":"k, accept the set as-is.
4. Otherwise require every answer to be public unicast, exactly as before."},{"id":"p19s1","text":"Step 3 is deliberately all-or-nothing. A placeholder carries no destination of
its own — only the lo"},{"id":"p19s2","text":"cal TUN adapter can route it — so accepting one does not
open a path to a private service. A **mixed"},{"id":"p19s3","text":"** set is refused because otherwise
a DNS answer could widen the policy by smuggling a private addre"},{"id":"p19s4","text":"ss alongside a
placeholder."},{"id":"p20s1","text":"### Why the stock row must be disabled"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"Both providers register the same fetch-provider id (`http`), and the web seam
rejects a duplicate wi"},{"id":"p21s2","text":"th `WEB_DUPLICATE_PROVIDER`. Disabling the row does not
remove the package — this plugin imports `Ht"},{"id":"p21s3","text":"tpFetchProvider` from it. Keeping
the same id means `ctx.web.fetch()` selects this provider under th"},{"id":"p21s4","text":"e existing
`fetchProvider: http` configuration, with no change to the web service row."},{"id":"p22s1","text":"## Security notes"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"This plugin exists because the stock check cannot be satisfied under fake-ip
DNS, so the question wo"},{"id":"p23s2","text":"rth asking is what the relaxation costs."},{"id":"p24s1","text":"**The relaxation is exactly as wide as the placeholder block.** Under fake-ip
the proxy performs ori"},{"id":"p24s2","text":"gin resolution, so upstream reachability is governed by
the proxy's own routing rules rather than by"},{"id":"p24s3","text":" this module. Two consequences:"},{"id":"p25s1","text":"- **Keep the proxy's rules from exposing private ranges** to the model's fetch
tool. A rule that rou"},{"id":"p25s2","text":"tes RFC1918 or loopback through the proxy would let a
hostname reach an internal service — that risk"},{"id":"p25s3","text":" is introduced by the proxy
configuration, not by this plugin, but the plugin is what makes the fetc"},{"id":"p25s4","text":"h
succeed, so it is worth auditing together.
- **IP literals are never placeholders.** They state a "},{"id":"p25s5","text":"destination the caller
chose, so handing one to a proxy running on this machine would reach exactly
"},{"id":"p25s6","text":"the loopback or private service the check exists to keep out of reach. This
is why `http://127.0.0.1"},{"id":"p25s7","text":"/` stays blocked even though a *hostname* that
resolves into the placeholder block does not."},{"id":"p26s1","text":"If you want a stricter posture, narrow `fakeIpRanges` to your proxy's exact
block (for example `198."},{"id":"p26s2","text":"18.0.0/16`) rather than the wider default."},{"id":"p27s1","text":"## Known limitations"},{"id":"p28s1","text":"- **The range must be configured by hand if it is not the default.** The plugin
cannot discover the "},{"id":"p28s2","text":"proxy's `dns.fake-ip-range`; `scripts/diagnose.mjs` tells
you what to set.
- **Only textual content "},{"id":"p28s3","text":"decodes** — inherited from the stock provider.
`text/html`, `application/xhtml+xml`, `text/*` and th"},{"id":"p28s4","text":"e JSON/XML families are
decoded; a missing `Content-Type` or a binary type throws
`WEB_UNSUPPORTED_C"},{"id":"p28s5","text":"ONTENT_TYPE`.
- **Charset comes only from the `Content-Type` header** (UTF-8 default) — also
inherit"},{"id":"p28s6","text":"ed; an HTML `<meta charset>` declaration is ignored.
- **The stock provider must be disabled.** Two "},{"id":"p28s7","text":"providers cannot share the
`http` id.
- **A future DSH line needs a peer-range update.** The declare"},{"id":"p28s8","text":"d range stops at
`0.3.0`, so a `0.3.x` harness skips this bundle until the range is widened.
That is"},{"id":"p28s9","text":" deliberate — an untested major line should be an explicit decision
rather than an assumed one — but"},{"id":"p28s10","text":" it does mean a DSH upgrade can require a
plugin update before `web_fetch` works again."}],"truncated":true}
